end.summary:
Defined health as physical, mental and social well-being, not only absence of disease.
Identified physical, mental and social as the three parts of health.
Connected food, sleep, walking, friendship and screen use to health with some prompting.
Daily-habit links remained incomplete; activity duration and replacing breakfast were uncertain.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Siya practised explaining the three parts of health using examples and a scenario about sleep, food and loneliness. They clearly explained that being free from disease alone does not mean being healthy, and connected sleep, walking, friendship and phone use to different parts of health. The mix-up about activity duration and whether a quick substitute is enough for breakfast was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Siya to sort five habits—food, sleep, activity, hygiene and screen use—under physical, mental or social health, allowing a habit to fit more than one category.
